request.spec:
The rollover now also soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open, in
start-date order, each as a soft close would (PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED), after the ROLLOVER line.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The rollover now also soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open, in
start-date order, each as a soft close would (PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED), after the ROLLOVER line.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Rolling a fiscal year over now also soft-closes every period of the old year that is still open, in start-date order. Each one writes a `PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED` line after the `ROLLOVER` line. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

**What changed**
- **New step `SoftCloseRollover.java`** (in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/period/`): runs after the existing carry step. For each old-year period, it re-reads the period's current state and skips any that are already closed or soft-closed. It soft-closes the rest using the same shared code a manual soft close uses, so the totals are fixed the same way, and it records the line as `PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED sheet=<id> by=<user> period=<name> total=<0.00>`.
- **`rollover.POST.yml`**: the new step is added to the rollover's steps, and the header comment now describes it.
- No front-end or stored-data changes were needed.

**One choice for you:** undoing a rollover still doesn't reopen the periods the rollover soft-closed, because the request didn't cover undo and the tests don't exercise it. If undo should reverse these soft closes, the rollover would also need to remember which periods it closed.

**One difference from a manual soft close:** the rollover doesn't check the sheet's role permissions for closing. Only a steward can roll over, so I treated that as enough.
